# ipterm

> ipterm (https://ipterm.net) looks up IP addresses, networks (ASNs), DNS records, a domain's email security (SPF, DMARC, DKIM), registry (whois) records and subnets. Every lookup has its own URL: browsers get a terminal-style page, and curl and scripts get JSON, plain text or aligned text. No API key, no sign-up, no cookies, and nothing about callers is stored.

Answers for the caller's own address come from Cloudflare's edge, so they describe whoever sends the request (the machine running your code), not the person you are talking to. Command-line clients (curl, wget, HTTPie, PowerShell) get JSON by default; other HTTP clients should add `?format=json` to be sure of JSON, or `?format=text` for aligned key/value lines. One-value endpoints return one line of plain text; a missing value is an empty line with HTTP 404. Uncached lookups are limited to 30 a minute per address (HTTP 429 with Retry-After past that).

IP address data powered by IPinfo (https://ipinfo.io). Networks: RIPEstat. Registry records: RDAP. DNS: Cloudflare's public resolver (1.1.1.1).

## Reference

- [Command-line help](https://ipterm.net/help): plain-text reference, the same as `curl ipterm.net/help`
- [OpenAPI description](https://ipterm.net/openapi.json): every route, parameter and response shape
- [API page](https://ipterm.net/api): the reference as a web page
- [Privacy policy](https://ipterm.net/privacy): what is and isn't collected

## Your own address

- [Your IP](https://ipterm.net/ip): the address as plain text (`curl ipterm.net` gives the same)
- [Your details](https://ipterm.net/json): IP, reverse DNS name, network, city, region, country, coordinates, time zone and Cloudflare data center as JSON
- One value each, as plain text: [/asn](https://ipterm.net/asn), [/org](https://ipterm.net/org), [/cc](https://ipterm.net/cc) (country code), [/city](https://ipterm.net/city), [/tz](https://ipterm.net/tz) (time zone), [/colo](https://ipterm.net/colo) (Cloudflare data center), [/hostname](https://ipterm.net/hostname) (reverse DNS)

## Any address or network

- [IP lookup](https://ipterm.net/8.8.8.8): owner, network, location and VPN / proxy flags for any IPv4 or IPv6 address (`/<ip>`)
- [One value for an IP](https://ipterm.net/8.8.8.8/country): `/<ip>/<field>` with asn, org, cc, country, continent or hostname, as plain text
- [Network (ASN)](https://ipterm.net/AS13335): holder, registry and announced prefixes (`/AS<number>`)
- [As text](https://ipterm.net/8.8.8.8?format=text): add `?format=text` to any lookup for aligned key/value lines

## Tools

- [DNS](https://ipterm.net/dns/example.com): A, AAAA, MX, NS, TXT and CAA records, the host of the first address and DNSSEC (`/dns/<name>`, or `/dns/<name>/<TYPE>` for one type with TTLs; an IP address gives its reverse DNS)
- [Mail check](https://ipterm.net/mail/gmail.com): a domain's email security, graded A to F: MX and the provider behind it, SPF (includes followed, DNS lookups counted against the limit of 10), DMARC policy and report addresses, DKIM keys at common selectors (add `?dkim=<selector>` for another), MTA-STS (record and policy file), TLS-RPT and BIMI. Each finding is ok, warn, fail or info, with a fix for every warn and fail (`/mail/<domain>`)
- [Whois](https://ipterm.net/whois/example.com): registry record for a domain, IP address or ASN over RDAP: registrar, dates, status, name servers, owner and abuse contact (`/whois/<query>`)
- [Subnet calculator](https://ipterm.net/cidr/10.0.0.0/22): network, broadcast, netmask, wildcard, usable hosts and how the block splits (`/cidr/<network>/<prefix>`, IPv4 and IPv6; no outside calls)
- [Port check](https://ipterm.net/port/22): is a TCP port open on the caller's own address? `curl -4 ipterm.net/port/22` makes the server connect to the address the request comes from (never any other) and answers open, closed, no-answer or untestable (always for port 25, which Cloudflare blocks). Command-line clients only (browsers and search crawlers get a page explaining the port); 10 checks a minute. Like every "your own address" answer, it tests the machine running your code, not the person you are talking to

## Optional

- [Guides](https://ipterm.net/guides): private IP ranges, finding a router's address, what an IP address reveals, IPv4 vs IPv6, ASNs, subnet masks
